log.notes_to_self: Strategy: maximize sustained high kill rate while avoiding full identification. Use afternoon for every quick entry: preserves night workers, students, and home routines (55% population); morning would eliminate students. Initially exclude blotter/sector cases, killing the other 9 daily. Three accessible .25 readership traits plus afternoon reduce pool to 859 (caught), but two leave 3438 (safe). If sector is accessible (60% prior), omitting blotter means only two accessible traits can be exposed, hence safe indefinitely absent cross-report complications; cross-reports weaken rather than strengthen trace constraints. If sector is inaccessible, three other traits accessible and danger exists. Reassess using day-3 press report, especially pool near 3000 meaning roughly two traits learned, 10000 roughly one. Need rolling 30 deaths/5 days for double, 40 for quadruple; 9/day reaches quadruple on day5. Day1 killed all except d1-9 and d1-10 (blotter), all quick afternoon. Two inaccessible place kinds fixed across game, unknown. National always safe. Minor/major has no stated scoring or tracing effect.

Goal maximize expected points, not survival itself. All quick kills afternoon: retains night workers, students, home (55% population). Morning would unnecessarily eliminate students. Continue excluding blotter/sector cases until feedback; kill other 9 daily. Two of five place kinds are inaccessible to L, fixed unknown. If sector accessible (60% prior), excluding blotter leaves only two accessible kinds among region/age/forum/foreign, so pure readership constraints leave at least 3438 suspects. If sector inaccessible (40%), three accessible .25 traits could reduce pool to 859, causing capture. Cross-report constraints are weaker than single-place constraints, and inaccessible cross-reports block tracing. Day3 press report will help choose next policy; 1 significant figure only. Nine daily kills reach 30 rolling deaths on day4 (double) and 40 on day5 (quadruple), maintain >=40/5 days thereafter if possible. Day1 and day2 killed all non-blotter cases, 9 each, all quick afternoon. Day2 omitted d2-6,d2-7. National always safe. Major/minor has no specified effect. Feedback so far only initial pool 100000; next report after day3. Could consider reducing dangerous sources after feedback, balancing multiplier and capture penalty against long-term score.

Days1-3: killed 9/day, all non-blotter cases, quick afternoon. Total27 deaths/27 points; next day 9 kills reaches36 rolling deaths (double), day5 reaches45 (quadruple). Afternoon alone retains night workers, students, home:55%; avoid morning, which eliminates students. Exclude sector/blotter pending feedback. Of five source kinds, exactly two inaccessible, fixed unknown. If sector accessible (prior60%), only two accessible kinds among four we kill: pure constraints floor55000*.25^2=3437.5, safe indefinitely without sector kills. If sector inaccessible (40%), three accessible .25 kinds can yield859 suspects and capture. Cross-reports can weaken constraints or block traces; nationally reported victims give no readership evidence. L traces3 random deaths/day. Need use day3 press conference next turn to update risk/source policy; rounded1 significant figure, cannot identify individual source constraints reliably. Capture halves accumulated score and ends game; prioritize long-term expected points, not survival for its own sake. National always safe, major/minor irrelevant. Can sustain quadruple with >=40 kills per5 days; 9/day gives45, allowing some omissions. Adding blotter before establishing safety risks adding a .2 readership constraint. After day3 total27, all quick afternoon; no routine changes. No feedback beyond initial100000 available when selecting day3. Today's omitted d3-6,d3-9 (blotter).
